core_obligations: Reduce to checking that the base change map induces an isomorphism on stalks at every point of the base change (proof lines 3121-3123).
Extract from properness the hypotheses needed on both sides of the square: the base changed map is proper, the fibres of both maps are quasi-compact and both maps are closed (proof lines 3124-3127).

Apply the fibre formula twice to identify the two sides with derived global sections over the corresponding fibres, and conclude because the induced map of fibres is a homeomorphism that pulls one restriction back to the other (proof lines 3128-3139).
proof_roadmap: Properness hypotheses on both sides (proof lines 3124-3127).
Two applications of the fibre formula and the homeomorphism of fibres (proof lines 3128-3139).
difficulty_reason: In a cartesian square of topological spaces with the vertical map proper, the theorem shows that the base change map relating the inverse image of the derived pushforward to the derived pushforward of the inverse image is an isomorphism for every bounded below complex (statement lines 3100-3119). The proof is a reduction to the pointwise statement: it suffices to check the map on stalks, properness is preserved by base change and supplies the closedness, separatedness and quasi-compact fibre hypotheses needed to apply the fibre formula for stalks of higher direct images on both sides of the square, and the two sides are then identified because the induced map of fibres is a homeomorphism pulling one restriction back to the other (proof lines 3121-3139). The claim is H2: no new construction, but the verification that the hypotheses of the fibre formula hold on both sides of the square is what makes the reduction work.
